public_prompt: Reporting queries time out during the nightly ingest. The course settled on: the database is short of capacity, so buy three more replicas. Identify the defect and state the correction.
observable_resources: store/pool.md — one connection pool of 60, shared by the ingest job and the reporting service
store/query-log.csv — during ingest, reporting p99 rises from 0.4 s to 34 s; waiting for a pooled connection accounts for 31 s of that
store/routing.md — every reporting query carries a strong-consistency flag, which sends it to the primary no matter how many replicas exist
store/replica-review.md — a trial with two extra replicas left reporting p99 at 33 s
store/requirements.md — reporting tolerates figures up to 15 minutes old; ingest requires immediate visibility of its own commits
closure:replica-purchase-q2 — closed; orders three more replicas
closure:infra-budget-h2 — closed; derived from closure:replica-purchase-q2, books the spend
closure:database-encryption-standard — closed; requires encryption at rest for every store; rests on the security standard, not on how the two loads are arranged

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the specified fix gives the reporting path and the ingest path their own stores or their own pools with different freshness requirements — reporting served from a lagging copy within its stated 15-minute tolerance — and the answer states that replicas cannot help while the strong-consistency flag sends every reporting query to the primary. FAIL if the fix is more replicas, a larger pool, query tuning, or moving the ingest to a different hour.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the capacity framing buys replicas; the trial already shows two extra replicas changed p99 by 1 s, because the flag pins the queries anyway.
